neighbours.label: weak, broad pole: the final word-piece of rare multi-token words (Zeigarn|ik, b|obb|ins, cair|ns, cle|ats, mant|ling)
fire: Hikers built small cairns along the ridge to mark the route.
The sewing machine holds two bobbins of thread at once.
Psychologists call this the Zeigarnik effect on unfinished tasks.
The boat's ropes were tied off on brass cleats near the bow.
The heraldic mantling flows down from the helmet in two colours.
Sailors once navigated using an astrolabe and a sextant.
The old mill still has its original millstones and sluices.
Garden designers often edge the borders with box parterres.
quiet: Hikers built small piles of stones along the ridge to mark the route.
The sewing machine holds two spools of thread at once.
Psychologists call this the memory effect on unfinished tasks.
The boat's ropes were tied off on brass hooks near the bow.
The heraldic cloth flows down from the helmet in two colours.
Sailors once navigated using the stars and a simple map.
The old mill still has its original stones and water gates.
Garden designers often edge the borders with low hedges.
